question.prompt:
How many of the twelve pentominoes pictured below have at least one line of symmetry?

[Figure 1](figures/2001_AMC_10_Q05_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
A line of symmetry is a fold line that makes the whole shape coincide with itself. Count each pentomino once if it has any such line, even when it has several.

[Figure 1](figures/2001_AMC_10_Q05_question_fig1.svg)

Number the columns from left to right. Checking the shapes row by row gives:

- Top row: only column 1 has symmetry. The straight strip folds along its length or across its middle.
- Middle row: all four have symmetry. Column 1 folds horizontally through its middle row of squares; column 2, the cross, folds vertically or horizontally; column 3 folds diagonally from upper right to lower left; column 4 folds vertically between its two legs.
- Bottom row: only column 1 has symmetry. Its diagonal fold exchanges the horizontal and vertical arms.

To check that none are missed, a symmetry axis for these shapes must be horizontal, vertical, or diagonal at \(45^\circ\), because reflection must match the horizontal and vertical boundary edges. Each axis must also pass through the center of the smallest enclosing rectangle. A diagonal axis is possible only when that enclosing rectangle is a square.

For the three rejected shapes in the top row and column 3 of the bottom row, the enclosing rectangles are not square. Their unequal top and bottom rows rule out a horizontal fold, and their off-center arrangements rule out a vertical fold. For columns 2 and 4 of the bottom row, testing both center lines and both diagonals leaves unmatched squares in every case. Thus the row counts include every symmetric shape exactly once.

The total is \(1+4+1=\boxed{6}\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
solutions.title: Check possible fold lines
